title: First Bad Version
statement: You are a quality-control engineer testing n versions of a product, numbered 1 to n in the order they were released. At some unknown version, the product became bad, and every version released after it is also bad. You are given n and the index bad (1-indexed) of the first bad version. Using only the fact that calling an internal check on version v tells you whether v is bad (v >= bad) or good (v < bad), find and return the smallest version number that is bad. You must not simply return bad directly from the input; instead, simulate calling the checker function isBadVersion(v) := v >= bad at most O(log n) times to locate the boundary via binary search on the answer.

hints: This is a 'binary search on the answer' problem: the search space is versions 1..n, not array indices into a data array.
The predicate is_bad(v) is monotonic — once it becomes True it stays True for all larger v — so binary search can find the boundary.
Keep a half-open range [lo, hi]; if mid is bad move hi down to mid, otherwise move lo up to mid + 1, until lo == hi.
